speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned experiencing double vision, difficulty climbing stairs, and upper limb weakness; to begin our evaluation, how long have these symptoms been present and are they constant or intermittent?

speaker: Patient
text: The double vision usually happens when I look up or down, and the weakness in my arms and legs gets worse after activity but improves if I rest. I have not noticed balance problems or numbness.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Myasthenia Gravis. The pattern of double vision triggered by eye movement and weakness that fluctuates with activity and improves with rest is classic for this autoimmune disorder affecting the neuromuscular junction. To confirm this, I will request a test for acetylcholine receptor antibodies.
